tips.title: Meilleur for nouns, mieux for verbs
tips.body: **Meilleur** is an adjective and describes a **noun**: *une meilleure solution*. **Mieux** is an adverb and describes a **verb**: *je mange mieux*. There is no *plus bon* or *plus bien*.

tips.title: Before and now needs two tenses
tips.body: *Avant, je **buvais** du coca, mais maintenant je **bois** de l'eau.* The imperfect for how things used to be, the present for how they are. That contrast is the whole task.

tips.title: Comparisons need que
tips.body: *Plus sain **que** avant*, *moins fatigué **que** l'année dernière*. Leaving out *que* leaves the comparison hanging and loses the mark.

steps.title: What a healthy lifestyle looks like
steps.body:
The last topic of the half term pulls the others together. You already have the words for feeling well and ill, and for resolutions. This topic adds the words for **habits**, and the grammar for saying how they have **changed**.

Two things to notice in the list below.

**Uncountable nouns stay singular**, as in English: *la malbouffe* is junk food, never *les malbouffes*.

**Adjectives still agree.** *Une alimentation équilibrée* takes the feminine *-e*, because *alimentation* is feminine. It sounds the same as the masculine and it is a written mark.

words.note: passer du temps sur les écrans

visuals.fallback: une alimentation équilibrée — a balanced diet; les fruits et légumes — fruit and vegetables; la malbouffe — junk food; les produits sucrés — sugary foods; les boissons gazeuses — fizzy drinks; grignoter — to snack; sédentaire — inactive; le tabac — tobacco; vapoter — to vape; les écrans — screens.

check.prompt: Which of these is junk food?
check.solution: **La malbouffe** is junk food. The others are green vegetables, mineral water and fresh fruit.

steps.title: Before and now: the imperfect against the present
steps.body:
Talking about a change means talking about **before**, and *used to* in French is the **imperfect**. You met it in Year 9; this is where it earns its keep.

The stem is the **nous** form of the present, minus **-ons**. Then one set of endings for every verb: **-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient**.

*Nous mangeons* → **mange-** → *je mangeais*. *Nous buvons* → **buv-** → *je buvais*. *Nous faisons* → **fais-** → *je faisais*.

The only irregular stem you need is **être**: *j'étais*.

One detail in *manger*: the **e** after the *g* is there only to keep the *g* soft before *a* or *o*. Before *i* it is soft already, so the *nous* and *vous* forms drop it: *nous mangions*.

Then the contrast writes itself: **avant**, imperfect; **maintenant**, present.

visuals.alt: A table of manger in the imperfect: je mangeais, tu mangeais, il mangeait, nous mangions, vous mangiez, ils mangeaient, with the endings highlighted

steps.text: Take the **nous** form of the present: *nous faisons*
Remove **-ons**: *fais-*
Add the ending: *je faisais* — *I used to do*
Only *être* breaks the rule: *j'étais*
steps.note: Every other verb, regular or not, follows the nous form

check.prompt: Write in French: *I used to eat*.
check.solution: **Je mangeais** — the stem *mange-* from *nous mangeons*, plus **-ais**.

steps.title: Comparing: plus, moins, aussi
steps.body:
A change is a comparison, so you need three words.

- **plus** … **que**: more … than — *les légumes sont **plus** sains **que** les frites*
- **moins** … **que**: less … than — *le coca est **moins** sain **que** l'eau*
- **aussi** … **que**: as … as — *le sommeil est **aussi** important **que** le sport*

The adjective in the middle **still agrees** with what it describes. *Les légumes* are masculine plural, so **sains**; *l'eau* is feminine, so **saine**.

With a **noun** rather than an adjective, it is **plus de** and **moins de**, with plain *de*: *je mange **plus de** fruits*, *je passe **moins de** temps sur les écrans*.

rows: moins de temps sur les écrans

visuals.alt: A table of the three comparative patterns with an example of each, plus the pattern with nouns

visuals.problem: Build: *Water is as important as sleep.*

steps.text: The pattern is **aussi** + adjective + **que**
steps.note: *aussi … que* for things that are equal

steps.text: The adjective agrees with *l'eau*, which is feminine: *importante*
steps.note: a silent **-e**, but a written mark

steps.text: *L'eau est aussi importante que le sommeil.*
With a noun the pattern changes: *je bois plus d'eau*
steps.note: **plus de** + noun; *de* elides to **d'** before a vowel

check.solution: *L'eau* is feminine, so **saine**; *than* is **que**. *La plus saine* would be *the healthiest*.

steps.title: Meilleur or mieux?
steps.body:
English has one word, *better*. French has two, and mixing them up is one of the commonest errors at this level.

**Meilleur** is an **adjective**. It describes a **noun** and agrees with it: *un meilleur repas*, *une **meilleure** solution*, *de **meilleurs** résultats*.

**Mieux** is an **adverb**. It describes a **verb** — how something is done — and never changes: *je dors **mieux***, *je mange **mieux** qu'avant*.

The test: ask *better what?* If the answer is a thing, it is **meilleur**. If it is how you do something, it is **mieux**.

And neither *plus bon* nor *plus bien* exists. *Good* and *well* have their own words for *better*, just as English does not say *gooder*.

visuals.alt: A table contrasting meilleur, an adjective that agrees with a noun, and mieux, an adverb that goes with a verb

visuals.problem: Build: *I sleep better and I eat better meals.*

steps.text: *Better* after *sleep* describes a verb, so **mieux**: *je dors mieux*
*Better meals* describes a noun, so **meilleur**, agreeing with *repas*: *de meilleurs repas*
*Je dors mieux et je mange de meilleurs repas.*
steps.note: two different words for one English word

steps.text: The test is *better what?* How I sleep, so **mieux**; better meals, so **meilleurs**

check.prompt: Complete: *Je mange ___ qu'avant* (I eat better than before).
check.solution: *Better* describes **how** you eat — a verb — so it is **mieux**, which never changes.

steps.title: Building a before-and-after answer
steps.body: Every writing and speaking task on this topic comes down to one move: say how you **used to** live, how you live **now**, and **why** it changed. Each piece is separately credited, and the tenses are what carry the range.

visuals.problem: From one clause to an answer that scores

steps.text: *Je mange bien.* — correct, one clause, one tense
*Avant, je mangeais mal, mais maintenant je mange bien.* — two time frames
steps.note: *Avant* and *maintenant* announce the tenses before the verb does

steps.text: *Avant, je mangeais beaucoup de malbouffe, mais maintenant je mange mieux car je veux être en forme.* — precise noun, *mieux*, and a reason
steps.note: *Beaucoup de* with plain *de*; *mieux* because it describes how you eat

steps.text: *…et je fais du sport depuis deux mois.* — *depuis* with the present
steps.note: Four structures a marker is looking for, in two sentences

check.solution: Only the first has two correct time frames, *mieux* used properly and a reason with *car*. The third makes *avant* present tense; the second and fourth pad with *bien*.
options: Avant je mangeais mal, mais maintenant je mange mieux car je veux être en forme
Je mange bien et c'est bien, et je mange bien parce que c'est bien pour moi
Avant je mange mal, mais maintenant je mange mieux car je veux être en forme
Je mangeais bien et je mangeais bien parce que manger bien est bien et sain

steps.title: Verbs that bring à or de
steps.body:
Many verbs that lead into an infinitive bring a small word with them, and it has to be learnt **with the verb**, because English gives no clue.

**+ de**: *arrêter **de***, *essayer **de***, *éviter **de***, *décider **de***, *oublier **de***.

**+ à**: *commencer **à***, *continuer **à***, *réussir **à***, *apprendre **à***.

**Nothing at all**: *aimer*, *vouloir*, *pouvoir*, *devoir*, *aller*, *préférer*, *espérer* — *je veux manger*, never *je veux de manger*.

When two such verbs follow each other, each keeps its own: *j'essaie **d'**arrêter **de** grignoter* — I am trying to stop snacking. The first *de* shortens to **d'** before the vowel.

**Il vaut mieux** + infinitive, *it is better to*, belongs here too. Like *il faut*, it never changes: *il vaut mieux boire de l'eau*.

visuals.fallback: arrêter de — to stop; essayer de — to try to; éviter de — to avoid; décider de — to decide to; commencer à — to start; continuer à — to carry on; réussir à — to manage to; il vaut mieux — it is better to; passer moins de temps sur — to spend less time on; en meilleure forme — in better shape.

visuals.problem: Build: *I have decided to stop vaping.*

steps.text: *Décider* brings **de**: *j'ai décidé de…*
*Arrêter* brings its own **de**: *arrêter de vapoter*
steps.note: each verb keeps its own little word

steps.text: *J'ai décidé d'arrêter de vapoter.*
Compare a verb that takes nothing: *je veux arrêter de vapoter*

check.skill: verbs followed by à or de

steps.title: Your turn: say how you have changed
steps.body:
Before the check, say three sentences aloud about your own habits: one with **avant** and the imperfect, one with **maintenant** and a comparison, one with **depuis**.

**Depuis** is the trap. English says *I **have been** doing sport for three months*, but the sport is still going on, so French uses the **present**: *je **fais** du sport depuis trois mois*. Putting it in the perfect tense changes the meaning to something that has finished.

visuals.fallback: Cover the English and test yourself on: une alimentation équilibrée, les fruits et légumes, la malbouffe, les produits sucrés, les boissons gazeuses, grignoter, arrêter de, essayer de, éviter de, décider de.

steps.text: English: *I have been doing sport for three months*
Is it still going on? Yes — so French uses the **present**
steps.note: Not the perfect, which would mean it has stopped

steps.text: *Je **fais** du sport **depuis** trois mois*

check.prompt: Translate into French: *I have been doing sport for three months.*
check.solution: **Je fais du sport depuis trois mois.** Still going on, so the **present** with **depuis**.

markScheme.description: je fais du sport depuis trois mois

accepted: je fais du sport depuis trois mois

steps.title: Going deeper: three time frames, and the superlative
steps.body:
This topic is where the half term's grammar comes together, and a grade 9 answer uses all of it.

**Three time frames in one paragraph.** *Avant*, imperfect. *Maintenant*, present. *À l'avenir*, simple future. Each signalled by its time phrase, so the examiner cannot miss the range.

**The superlative.** *Le plus* / *la plus* / *les plus* + adjective: *le sport le plus utile*. When the adjective comes **after** the noun, the article appears twice: *la boisson **la** plus saine*. And the superlative of *bon* is **le meilleur**, agreeing: *la meilleure décision*.

**The traps that cost marks here**:

1. **meilleur** with nouns, **mieux** with verbs — never *plus bon*, never *plus bien*.
2. **plus de** and **moins de** with a noun take plain *de*.
3. **depuis** + present for something still going on.
4. the **à** or **de** that belongs to the verb, twice over when verbs are chained.

visuals.problem: Three time frames in one answer

steps.text: *Avant, j'étais sédentaire et je passais des heures sur les écrans.* — imperfect
*Maintenant, je fais du sport depuis deux mois et je me sens en meilleure forme.* — present, with *depuis*
*À l'avenir, j'essaierai de manger plus sainement, car c'est la meilleure décision pour ma santé.* — simple future, and a superlative
Three tenses, a comparison, a superlative and a reason
steps.note: This is the shape of a top-band answer at the end of Autumn 1

visuals.alt: A table of the superlative patterns with examples

check.solution: *Décision* is a feminine noun, so **meilleure** — an adjective, agreeing. *Mieux* cannot go with a noun, and *plus bonne* does not exist.
options: C'est la meilleure décision que j'ai prise pour ma santé
C'est la mieux décision que j'ai prise pour ma santé
C'est la meilleur décision que j'ai prise pour ma santé
C'est la plus bonne décision que j'ai prise pour ma santé

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Habits vocabulary**: *une alimentation équilibrée*, *la malbouffe*, *les boissons gazeuses*, *grignoter*, *sédentaire*, *les écrans*.
- **The imperfect** for *used to*: the *nous* stem minus *-ons*, then *-ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient*. Only *être* is irregular: *j'étais*.
- **Before and now**: *avant* + imperfect, *maintenant* + present.
- **Comparing**: *plus / moins / aussi* + adjective + *que*, and the adjective agrees. With a noun: *plus de*, *moins de*, plain *de*.
- **Better**: **meilleur** with nouns, agreeing; **mieux** with verbs, never changing. No *plus bon*, no *plus bien*.
- **Superlative**: *le / la / les plus* + adjective; after the noun, the article twice — *la boisson la plus saine*.
- **Verbs with à or de**: *arrêter de, essayer de, éviter de, décider de; commencer à, continuer à, réussir à*. Learn the word with the verb.
- **Il vaut mieux** + infinitive: *it is better to*. Never changes.
- **Depuis** + present for something still going on: *je fais du sport depuis trois mois*.
- **Range**: imperfect, present and simple future in one answer, each with its time phrase.

rows: il vaut mieux boire de l'eau
je fais du sport depuis trois mois

questions.solution: **La malbouffe** is *junk food*: *mal* (badly) + *bouffe* (slang for food). Like *junk food* it is uncountable, so it never takes a plural.
**Les boissons gazeuses** are fizzy drinks. The others are dairy products, seafood and ready meals — all common in the reading paper as distractors.

questions.prompt: Translate into English: **je mange des fruits et des légumes**.
questions.solution: *I eat fruit and vegetables.* French needs **des** in front of each noun; English needs no article at all.
**Sédentaire** means *inactive* or *sedentary* — a cognate once you know it. It is the same in the masculine and the feminine.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: **I used to eat a lot of sweets.**
questions.solution: **Je mangeais beaucoup de bonbons.** *Used to* is the imperfect: **je mangeais**, keeping the **e** so the *g* stays soft. And **beaucoup de**, never *des*.

questions.prompt: Complete: *Les légumes sont ___ que les frites.*
questions.solution: **Plus sains.** The adjective still agrees in a comparison: *légumes* is masculine plural, so **sains**.

questions.prompt: Complete with the missing word: *Je vais essayer ___ manger moins de sucre.*
questions.skill: verbs followed by à or de
questions.solution: **de** — *essayer de* + infinitive. The preposition belongs to the verb and has to be learnt with it.
*Better* describing a **verb** — how you sleep — is **mieux**, and it never changes. **Meilleur** describes a noun. *Plus bon* and *plus bien* do not exist.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: **I have been eating more healthily for two months.**
questions.solution: **Je mange plus sainement depuis deux mois.** *Have been doing* with **depuis** is the **present** in French, because the eating is still going on. **Sainement** is the adverb from *sain*.

markScheme.description: je mange … depuis deux mois, in the present

accepted: je mange plus sainement depuis deux mois
depuis deux mois je mange plus sainement
je mange plus sainement depuis 2 mois
depuis 2 mois je mange plus sainement

questions.prompt: Which is the imperfect of *manger* for **nous**?
questions.solution: **Nous mangions.** The extra **e** only appears before *a* or *o*, to keep the *g* soft; before *i* it is soft already, so *mangions* has none. *Nous mangeions* is not a real form, which is the trap; the other two are the perfect and the future.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: **Before, I used to drink a lot of fizzy drinks, but now I drink water.**
questions.solution: **Avant, je buvais beaucoup de boissons gazeuses, mais maintenant je bois de l'eau.** The imperfect **je buvais** comes from *nous buvons*; the present **je bois** is irregular. **Beaucoup de** takes plain *de*, and *water* needs the partitive: **de l'eau**.
accepted: avant je buvais beaucoup de boissons gazeuses mais maintenant je bois de l'eau

questions.solution: An adjective that comes **after** the noun keeps its place, and the article is said twice: **la boisson la plus saine**. *La boisson plus saine* is not French at all; *a healthier drink* is *une boisson plus saine*, with a single article.

questions.prompt: Translate into French: **It is better to eat fruit.**
questions.solution: **Il vaut mieux manger des fruits.** **Il vaut mieux** + infinitive means *it is better to*, and like *il faut* it never changes. *Fruit* needs **des** in French.
accepted: il vaut mieux manger des fruits

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the three time frames correctly?
questions.solution: **Avant** takes the imperfect, **maintenant** the present, **à l'avenir** the simple future. And *better* with a verb is **mieux**, so the third sentence fails on *meilleur*.
options: Avant je mangeais mal, maintenant je mange bien et à l'avenir je mangerai mieux
Avant je mange mal, maintenant je mangeais bien et à l'avenir je mangerai mieux
Avant je mangeais mal, maintenant je mange bien et à l'avenir je mangerai meilleur
Avant je mangerai mal, maintenant je mange bien et à l'avenir je mangeais mieux

questions.prompt: Translate into French: **I am going to try to stop snacking.**
questions.skill: verbs followed by à or de
questions.solution: **Je vais essayer d'arrêter de grignoter.** Two verbs in a row each bring their own **de**: *essayer **de***, then *arrêter **de***. The first *de* elides before the vowel: **d'arrêter**.
accepted: je vais essayer d'arrêter de grignoter
je vais essayer d'arreter de grignoter

questions.solution: *Solution* is a feminine noun, so the adjective is **meilleure**. **Mieux** goes with verbs, not nouns, and *plus bonne* does not exist.

questions.prompt: Écrivez environ 80 mots en français sur votre mode de vie. Mentionnez: comment vous viviez avant · ce que vous faites maintenant · ce que vous changerez à l'avenir.
questions.solution: Level-marked on content and language. A strong answer covers all three bullet points, each in its own tense — imperfect, present, simple future — signalled by *avant*, *maintenant* and *à l'avenir*. It uses a comparative, a verb that takes *à* or *de*, and a reason with *parce que* or *car*.

markScheme.description: Content: all three bullet points covered, with some development
Language: three time frames, accurate verb forms, range of structures

criteria.text: All three bullet points covered, each developed rather than listed
The imperfect for before, the present for now and the simple future for later, all correct
A comparative or superlative, with meilleur or mieux used correctly
A verb followed by à or de, and a reason with parce que or car

questions.modelAnswer: Avant, je mangeais beaucoup de malbouffe et je passais trois heures par jour sur les écrans. J'étais souvent fatigué parce que je ne faisais pas de sport. Maintenant, j'essaie de manger plus sainement et je fais du vélo depuis deux mois, donc je me sens en meilleure forme. À l'avenir, j'arrêterai de grignoter entre les repas et je dormirai mieux, car à mon avis il vaut mieux se coucher tôt.

questions.prompt: Traduisez en français: *I have been doing more sport for two months. Before, I used to spend three hours on screens every evening. Next year I will try to sleep better.*
questions.solution: **Je fais plus de sport depuis deux mois. Avant, je passais trois heures sur les écrans tous les soirs. L'année prochaine, j'essaierai de mieux dormir.** The traps: *have been doing* with **depuis** is the present; **plus de** takes plain *de*; *used to* is the imperfect **passais**; *try to* is **essayer de**; and *better* with a verb is **mieux**.

trois heures sur les écrans tous les soirs

Avant, je passais trois heures sur les écrans tous les soirs, in the imperfect
L'année prochaine, j'essaierai de mieux dormir, with essayer de and mieux

examTechnique.body:
This topic closes the first half term, and it is where the grammar of the three before it has to work together. Almost every question — written, spoken or translated — is some version of *how did you live before, how do you live now, what will you change?*, and that question is built to be answered in three tenses.

The marks split between content and language. Content means answering every part of the task with development. Language means range, and here range is concrete: the imperfect, the present and the simple future, a comparison, a superlative, a verb that brings *à* or *de*. A short answer that has all of those beats a long one that stays in the present.

In translation into French, most marks are lost on small words: *de* after quantities, the *à* or *de* after a verb, and *mieux* where *meilleur* was needed. Read the finished sentence back for each of those before moving on.
examinerErrors: Writing *plus bon* or *plus bien*. The words are **meilleur** (with a noun) and **mieux** (with a verb).
Using *mieux* with a noun, as in *la mieux solution*. With a noun it is **la meilleure solution**, and it agrees.
Forgetting that the adjective agrees inside a comparison: *les légumes sont plus **sains***, *l'eau est plus **saine***.
Putting *depuis* with the perfect tense for something still going on. *I have been doing sport for three months* is *je **fais** du sport depuis trois mois*.
Dropping or swapping the preposition after a verb: *j'essaie **de***, *je commence **à***, and none after *vouloir*, *pouvoir* or *aimer*.
Writing *beaucoup des* or *moins des*. Quantity words always take plain **de**.
Leaving *avant* in the present tense. *Used to* is the imperfect: *avant, je **mangeais***.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer on lifestyle moves through three time frames in a short paragraph — imperfect after *avant*, present after *maintenant*, simple future after *à l'avenir* — so the range is unmistakable. It compares with the adjective agreeing, uses *meilleur* and *mieux* correctly without hesitating, and reaches for a superlative once, with the article repeated after the noun. Verbs that take *à* or *de* are chained correctly, *depuis* sits with the present, and every opinion has a reason.
